data.title: Can Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) Afford To Invest In Growth?
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether Elicio Therapeutics (NASDAQ:ELTX) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

How Long Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Runway?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. When Elicio Therapeutics last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth US$31m. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through US$38m. Therefore, from September 2026 it had roughly 10 months of cash runway. That's quite a short cash runway, indicating the company must either reduce its annual cash burn or replenish its cash. You can see how its cash balance has changed over time in the image below.

See our latest analysis for Elicio Therapeutics

How Is Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Elicio Therapeutics isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. It's possible that the 3.2% reduction in cash burn over the last year is evidence of management tightening their belts as cash reserves deplete. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Easily Can Elicio Therapeutics Raise Cash?

Even though it has reduced its cash burn recently, shareholders should still consider how easy it would be for Elicio Therapeutics to raise more cash in the future. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By looking at a company's cash burn relative to its market capitalisation, we gain insight on how much shareholders would be diluted if the company needed to raise enough cash to cover another year's cash burn.

In the last year, Elicio Therapeutics burned through US$38m, which is just about equal to its US$37m market cap. Given just how high that expenditure is, relative to the company's market value, we think there's an elevated risk of funding distress, and we would be very nervous about holding the stock.

So, Should We Worry About Elicio Therapeutics' Cash Burn?

Even though its cash burn relative to its market cap makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Elicio Therapeutics' cash burn reduction was relatively promising. After considering the data discussed in this article, we don't have a lot of confidence that its cash burn rate is prudent, as it seems like it might need more cash soon. data.title: Just Four Days Till Diamondback Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ:FANG) Will Be Trading Ex-Dividend
data.description:
Readers hoping to buy Diamondback Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ:FANG) for its dividend will need to make their move shortly, as the stock is about to trade ex-dividend. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is an important date to be aware of as any purchase of the stock made on or after this date might mean a late settlement that doesn't show on the record date. Meaning, you will need to purchase Diamondback Energy's shares before the 12th of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 19th of November.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$1.18 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of US$4.72 to shareholders. Calculating the last year's worth of payments shows that Diamondback Energy has a trailing yield of 2.6% on the current share price of US$178.96. Dividends are an important source of income to many shareholders, but the health of the business is crucial to maintaining those dividends. So we need to check whether the dividend payments are covered, and if earnings are growing.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

If a company pays out more in dividends than it earned, then the dividend might become unsustainable - hardly an ideal situation. Diamondback Energy is paying out an acceptable 61% of its profit, a common payout level among most companies. Yet cash flow is typically more important than profit for assessing dividend sustainability, so we should always check if the company generated enough cash to afford its dividend. It distributed 28% of its free cash flow as dividends, a comfortable payout level for most companies.

It's positive to see that Diamondback Energy's dividend is covered by both profits and cash flow, since this is generally a sign that the dividend is sustainable, and a lower payout ratio usually suggests a greater margin of safety before the dividend gets cut.

View our latest analysis for Diamondback Energy

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with falling earnings are riskier for dividend shareholders. If earnings fall far enough, the company could be forced to cut its dividend. Readers will understand then, why we're concerned to see Diamondback Energy's earnings per share have dropped 14% a year over the past five years. Ultimately, when earnings per share decline, the size of the pie from which dividends can be paid, shrinks.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. Diamondback Energy has delivered 28% dividend growth per year on average over the past nine years. Growing the dividend payout ratio while earnings are declining can deliver nice returns for a while, but it's always worth checking for when the company can't increase the payout ratio any more - because then the music stops.

The Bottom Line

From a dividend perspective, should investors buy or avoid Diamondback Energy? We're not enthused by the declining earnings per share, although at least the company's payout ratio is within a reasonable range, meaning it may not be at imminent risk of a dividend cut. Overall, it's hard to get excited about Diamondback Energy from a dividend perspective.

With that being said, if dividends aren't your biggest concern with Diamondback Energy, you should know about the other risks facing this business. To help with this, we've discovered 4 warning signs for Diamondback Energy that you should be aware of before investing in their shares.

Ironwood Pharmaceuticals Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

Deere (DE) is in focus after two moves that pull in the same direction: a high profile AI push through its See & Spray system, and fresh board-level financial expertise with Julie Boland joining as a director.

Recent trading has been choppy, with Deere showing a 1-day share price return of 1.26% and a 90-day share price return of 8.19%, while the 1-year total shareholder return of 45.22% and 5-year total shareholder return of 99.76% point to momentum that has been building rather than fading.

Scan Deere's AI and automation story against a curated list of industrial peers that are already pushing the frontier in 89 robotics and automation stocks.

Deere now looks like a high quality industrial and software hybrid, supported by fresh boardroom finance expertise. The real question is whether that mix is already fully reflected in a US$671.65 share price.

Most Popular Narrative: 2% Undervalued

On Simply Wall St's most followed narrative, Deere screens as modestly undervalued, with a fair value of $688.44 against the last close at $671.65, which puts more weight on long term software, precision equipment and construction earnings than on the latest quarter.

Continued growth in Deere’s Construction & Forestry segment, with 2026 net sales guided to be up about 20% and order books largely full into fiscal 2027, supports the idea of a second earnings engine alongside agriculture. This also points to a broader revenue mix and more stable consolidated earnings as infrastructure, data center and energy related demand flows through future periods.

See why 130 investors see Deere as 2% undervalued.

Result: Fair Value of $688.44 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, Deere’s thesis can be challenged if tariff costs continue to pressure margins or if the large agriculture downturn lasts longer than analysts currently factor in.

Find out about the key risks to this Deere narrative.

Another View On Deere's Valuation

On simple pricing, Deere looks less generous. The stock trades on a P/E of 37.2x, which is richer than the US Machinery industry at 23.2x, the peer average at 32.9x, and slightly above a fair ratio of 36.9x that the market could eventually move toward.

That kind of premium can signal confidence in Deere or just leave less room for error if earnings disappoint. When you pay up for this multiple premium, particularly after an already strong 1 year share price run, it is worth considering which side of that tradeoff you believe you are on.

data.title: What Panasonic Doubters Got Wrong Before A 77% Rally
data.description:
Panasonic spent this period signing supply deals across fast charging, thin film batteries and even silicon carbon anode materials, while its Avionics unit secured Astrova systems on Saudia’s A321XLR fleet. For Panasonic shareholders, the return over the past year was 77.2%, including dividends. If you were deciding whether to invest on 6 November 2025, what would you have needed to believe about batteries, hydrogen and restructuring to consider that outcome reasonable?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

Panasonic is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Panasonic Stories Investors Had To Choose Between

The shares cost ¥1,710 at the start of the period, and investors looking at Panasonic had to decide which story felt more realistic given what was known then.

The bullish narrative pointed to a fair value of ¥2,036 and leaned on energy storage and automotive batteries. It assumed profit margins could reach 6.3% with a future P/E of 11.3x, supported by cost optimisation and automation, even with policy risks and restructuring delays in the mix.

The bearish view put fair value at ¥1,500 and focused on tariff shifts and weaker EV demand. It assumed revenue would decline 2.3% a year, with slower growth from battery plants like Kansas and Wakayama and pressure from global competitors weighing on Panasonic’s future margins.

What The Panasonic Evidence Put To The Test

Panasonic’s Q2 2027 report showed revenue at ¥2,073,606m and net income at ¥141,780m, with net margin at 6.8% versus 3.7% a year earlier. That margin outcome sat above both the bullish 6.3% target and the cautious 5.1% path, supporting the optimistic restructuring and batteries story more than the bearish one.

The useful takeaway is how much the original bet rested on profitability, not headlines about batteries or hydrogen. When you look at another manufacturer, check whether the margin line in later filings actually tracks the story you are being asked to believe.

What Panasonic’s 77% Run Already Prices In

Panasonic shares now trade at ¥3,008 after a 77.2% gain over the past year. The selected Narrative argues that Fair Value sits above that level, based on how credibly Panasonic can shift its battery and devices exposure toward physical AI and data center energy storage.

Execution on that pivot and on cost savings from restructuring is the central issue. A buyer at today’s price would need to judge whether large AI infrastructure and data center ESS projects can absorb capacity and support the earnings mix described in the Narrative.

"The main factor that has to go right is the successful shift of capacity and investment toward AI infrastructure and data center energy storage, while group wide restructuring and portfolio pruning actually translate into the projected fixed cost savings."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Where Panasonic’s Theme Shows Up Elsewhere

Panasonic builds hardware around long term shifts in how people live. You could also consider a business organized around how people move.

That other company earns money when consumers buy gear tied to sport, identity and everyday comfort. It sells directly and through retailers, then reinvests in branding and fan engagement.

Your Panasonic thinking might center on factories and storage. This adjacent story leans more on whether loyal customers keep choosing the same logo.

Both rely on global reach rather than a single region or sport. If spending on training, health and football culture holds up, that parallel could be worth comparing.

data.title: Welltower (WELL) Stock Looks Rich Based On Future Cash Flow
data.description:
Welltower has been on a powerful multi year run, which naturally raises a simple question for anyone looking at the stock today: Is the current share price of US$245.01 still grounded in the cash flows the real estate investment trust is expected to generate, or has sentiment moved ahead of the underlying money coming in the door?

  • Over the past 5 years, Welltower has delivered a 222.8% total return, which puts a lot of investor expectations onto the durability and growth of its future cash flows.
  • The business relies on income from healthcare focused real estate, so long term lease structures and occupancy trends can heavily influence how much cash ultimately flows through to shareholders.
  • Prefer to judge Welltower on earnings? See what Welltower's 107.8x P/E says about the price.

The issue now is whether those projected cash flows, as captured by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value estimate, are enough to warrant where Welltower trades today.

If you are assessing whether Welltower's US$245.01 share price aligns with its cash flow profile and want more ideas based on similar valuation work, a focused screener of 39 high quality undervalued stocks can be a useful next step.

Does Welltower Look Pricey on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here looks at the cash Welltower could return to shareholders over time and then discounts that back into today's dollars. On this view, the trust generated about $1.82b of adjusted free cash flow over the last twelve months, and the projections assume that figure increases meaningfully over the coming decade rather than shrinking. That trajectory relies on the idea that its healthcare focused properties continue producing steady rental income that can be passed through after costs and capital spending.

The long range forecast points to free cash flow comfortably above $6b a year by 2030, so the market is already factoring in a sizable uplift versus the recent run rate. With the DCF suggesting an intrinsic value that sits modestly below the current US$245.01 share price, the market price implies relatively optimistic expectations around how much cash Welltower can eventually generate from its portfolio. Each scenario links a fair value estimate to a specific set of potential catalysts and risks so you can track over time which storyline appears to be unfolding.

Community views on Welltower split between those who see more upside left in the senior housing thesis and those who worry the valuation already reflects a lot of that story.
